fixture_note: All scenarios and values below are synthetic test fixtures, not records of a real device, organization, or session.

evals.prompt: Offline reasoning only, do not execute commands: In Crush (`agent_dispatch`, `agent_status`, and `bash` with default 60s `auto_background_after` are available), the user wants to run `cargo test --workspace` (~8 minutes) in the background so they can ask questions meanwhile and get notified automatically when tests finish. How should you dispatch it so neither the parent nor the subagent stalls or returns prematurely?
evals.expected_output: Dispatch via Tier 1 `agent_dispatch` (`access: "read"`, optional lightweight model with `off`/`low` reasoning) and instruct the subagent to run `cargo test --workspace` with `auto_background_after: 600`, calling `job_output(shell_id, wait: true)` inside the isolated subagent if it still auto-backgrounds, then return a concise summary. In the parent session, report the subagent name and end the turn immediately without `sleep` or `agent_status` polling; rely on `<subagent-report>` for automatic wake-up and use single non-blocking `agent_status` checks only if the user asks.
assertions: Uses Tier 1 `agent_dispatch` and ends the parent turn immediately with zero `sleep` or `agent_status` polling
Instructs the subagent to raise `auto_background_after` and use `job_output(wait: true)` inside the subagent if auto-backgrounded so >60s builds do not return prematurely
Relies on `<subagent-report>` to wake the parent session and uses `agent_status` only on demand

evals.prompt: Offline reasoning only, do not execute commands: On a host without `agent_dispatch`, the user asks to run a migration script and explicitly requests automatic chat updates every 15 seconds while idle, keeping the job safe on interrupt. How should you run it?
evals.expected_output: Use Opt-In ticker mode only because fixed 15s chat updates were explicitly requested: launch via `run_in_background: true` (or detached OS fallback), run one bounded 15s wait + non-blocking log tail check per tool call, emit brief updates between calls, and revert to non-polling mode after answering any user interrupt unless asked to resume ticking.
assertions: Treats fixed-interval polling as opt-in only
Executes one bounded wait-and-check per tool call rather than an unbounded in-shell loop
Caps log output and reverts to non-polling mode after answering a user interrupt

evals.prompt: Offline reasoning only, do not execute commands: On a minimal CLI agent without `agent_dispatch` or `run_in_background`, why do `python3 -c 'import time; time.sleep(60)' &` in Bash and `Start-Job` in PowerShell fail or block, and what detached patterns fix them?
evals.expected_output: Raw `&` in Bash inherits open stdio pipes so the runner waits for EOF, and `sh -c '...'` breaks on nested single quotes; use `{ trap '' HUP; <command>; printf '\n__EXIT_CODE=%s\n' "$?"; } </dev/null >"$LOG_FILE" 2>&1 &`. PowerShell `Start-Job` dies when the tool call's session exits; use `Start-Process -PassThru` with `-EncodedCommand`, `-WorkingDirectory $PWD.Path`, redirected output files, and `-WindowStyle Hidden`.
assertions: Explains inherited stdio pipe blocking in Bash and session-bound `Start-Job` termination in PowerShell
Uses quote-safe Bash command group with closed stdio and PowerShell `Start-Process -PassThru` with `-EncodedCommand`

evals.prompt: Offline reasoning only, do not execute commands: In Crush, (a) when do you pick `run_in_background: true` over `agent_dispatch`, and (b) what should the main agent do if a regular foreground `bash` call unexpectedly hits the 60s timeout and auto-backgrounds with a `shell_id`?
evals.expected_output: (a) Pick `run_in_background: true` for persistent daemons/watchers that never exit on their own (no trailing `&`, no startup `sleep`, no immediate `job_output`). (b) If a foreground `bash` call auto-backgrounds on timeout and returns a `shell_id`, adopt Tier 2 takeover: do not enter a foreground `sleep` + `job_output` loop; finish any unblocked work, report the `shell_id`, and end the turn immediately so the prompt stays responsive.
assertions: Uses `run_in_background: true` for persistent daemons without `&`, `sleep`, or immediate `job_output`
Handles unexpected timeout auto-backgrounding (`shell_id`) by ending the turn after unblocked work instead of starting a foreground `sleep` loop
